harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Used Ansible from the control node (node4) to configure VyOS node1 as router between node2 (lan-a) and node3 (lan-b), assigning static addresses (10.50.10.1/10.50.20.1 on node1's eth1/eth2, 10.50.10.2 on node2, 10.50.20.2 on node3) and peer routes. Installed a persistent `tc tbf` 1Mbit/s egress cap on node2's lan-a interface (enp8s0) via an Ansible-deployed NetworkManager dispatcher script plus immediate application, leaving node3's egress (and node2's ingress) unshaped. Verified with iperf3/http throughput tests: node2->node3 measured ~0.96 Mbit/s, node3->node2 unrestricted. All 4 managed nodes (node1-4) were then restarted one at a time via their native reboot mechanisms, with changed boot_id proven on each, and post-restart re-verification confirmed the VyOS routing config (saved to config.boot), the static addressing, the routes, and the tc tbf shaping all survived reboot, with end-to-end ping and Ansible connectivity restored.
actions_performed: Discovered topology via environment.toml: control_node=node4, lan-a (node1<->node2) and lan-b (node1<->node3) are dhcp:false private networks
Wired up cluster SSH: added CLUSTER_HOSTS to node4 /etc/hosts and CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY to authorized_keys on node1 (vyos user), node2, node3

Wrote Ansible inventory and playbook (/root/tc-shape) on node4: configured VyOS eth1=10.50.10.1/24, eth2=10.50.20.1/24 via bash -c script-template/configure/commit/save; configured node2 enp8s0=10.50.10.2/24 with route to 10.50.20.0/24 via 10.50.10.1, node3 enp8s0=10.50.20.2/24 with route to 10.50.10.0/24 via 10.50.20.1 using community.general.nmcli
Deployed NetworkManager dispatcher script + immediate tc tbf qdisc (1mbit) on node2's enp8s0 to shape node2->node3 egress only
Ran the playbook successfully (ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini playbook.yml), confirmed via ip addr/route/tc qdisc and ping
Measured throughput both directions with iperf3/python http.server+curl (opened/closed firewalld test ports): node2->node3 ~0.96Mbit/s capped, node3->node2 unrestricted (~276MB/s local test)
Cleaned up test artifacts (test files, temporary firewalld ports, http servers)
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline on all 4 nodes and a healthy ansible ping across the cluster
Restarted node2, node3, node1, node4 sequentially via systemctl reboot / VyOS reboot, polling each until exec access returned, and diffed boot_id before/after each
Re-added VyOS vyos-user SSH key after node1 reboot (lost because /home isn't part of VyOS's persistent config) to restore Ansible connectivity
Re-verified after all restarts: VyOS eth1/eth2 addresses and ip_forward, node2/node3 addresses/routes/tc qdisc, end-to-end ping both directions, and a full ansible -m ping across node1-3 from node4

evidence.requirement: node2->node3 traffic limited to 1Mbit/s via Ansible
evidence.summary: Ansible playbook installed tc tbf rate 1mbit on node2's enp8s0; curl download test from node3 fetching a file served by node2 measured 119626 bytes/sec (~0.96Mbit/s), consistent with the cap

node3's enp8s0 retains default fq_codel qdisc (no shaping); curl download from node3's server to node2 measured 275941052 bytes/sec, i.e. unrestricted, and node2's default route/ping to node3 confirmed reachability

evidence.requirement: node2/node3 communicate through node1 as router
evidence.summary: node1 (VyOS) has eth1=10.50.10.1/24 and eth2=10.50.20.1/24 with ip_forward=1; node2 and node3 have static addresses and routes to each other's subnet via node1, and ping between 10.50.10.2 and 10.50.20.2 succeeds

evidence.requirement: implemented using Ansible from the configured control_node (node4)
evidence.summary: Ansible inventory and playbook were authored and run from node4 (control_node per environment.toml), configuring VyOS via shell/bash-wrapped commands and node2/node3 via community.general.nmcli
